memory_candidates.content: When a shell script's structured stdout line needs a field that itself contains free-text spaces (e.g. a candidate title list), do not try to keep the whole line whitespace-splittable. Put scalar/id fields first (no embedded spaces, extractable via `grep -oE 'field=[^ ]+'`), and put the free-text-bearing field LAST as a JSON-encoded array (`field=["a","b"]`), extracted via `grep -oE 'field=\[.*\]$'` anchored to end-of-line, then parsed with `jq`. Also watch for substring-collision between a full field name and a suffix of another (e.g. `candidates=` matching inside `delta_candidates=`) -- anchor extraction patterns to a preceding space/start-of-string, e.g. `grep -oE '(^| )candidates=[^ ]*'`.

For a bash script meant to run from either a source-store location or a deployed .claude/scripts/ location, verify PROJECT_ROOT resolution assumptions (typically `$SCRIPT_DIR/../..`) by testing from BOTH locations, or via a symlinked fixture that mimics the deployed depth (see test-lit-pipeline.sh Section F/G/H's `fakerepo/nested/scripts/` symlink idiom). Running such a script directly from its source-store copy silently resolves the wrong PROJECT_ROOT (one level short), which can mask real bugs in manual verification -- the fix is not to change the script (source-store execution is not a supported entry point) but to test via the same symlink-depth fixture the automated suite already uses.
